description: Ten days, and the glass turned

participation.context: Counted ten days with the sermon and did not call across to the Mayor's pew.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Turned the sand-glass twice and sent the parish to dinner with the number ten.
participation.name: Master Josias Thwaite

participation.context: Waited the second glass and kept Alse from treating the sermon as a wait for the loaf.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Named the short loaf and Sir John's unturned head, and remembered ten.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

participation.context: Sat three rows ahead in the carved pew and did not speak.
participation.name: Sir John Spencer

relations.note: she expects the second turning and waits for it

story.body: You stood the two turnings. You heard ten days to the fast. You left Sir John his pew, and you went to dinner with the house.

relations.note: she expects the second turning and waits for it

title: Heard Master Thwaite say the fast was ten days off

description: A penny, and a finger short

participation.context: Paid threepence and sixpence, and refused to open the Sunday letter again.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Laid the loaf against the notch, took the week's sixpence once, and said she would count the spoons after dinner.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Named the finger short, and said she would rather find a spoon than discuss one.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

participation.context: Sat at the end of the bench, nodded at the loaf, and did not speak.
participation.name: Gillis Verbeke

relations.note: the week's firing is taken once, at table
relations.quote: I will have it once, not once at dinner and once at the stair.

story.body: You paid threepence and the week's sixpence, once. You left the letter folded for Thursday. You went up before the spoons were counted.

relations.note: the week's firing is taken once, at table
relations.quote: I will have it once, not once at dinner and once at the stair.

topics: the spoon count still to come

title: Paid the meal and the week's sixpence

participation.context: Asked which caller could profit by a spoon, and took the kitchen as the answer.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Counted one short, accused nobody, and said the spoon had been put there to be found.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Found it among the ink-things, black to the neck, and set it on the board beside the pot.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

relations.note: she finds the spoon in her mistress's own ink-things
relations.quote: It is here. In with the ink-things.

story.body: You asked the question and did not supply a name. Alse found the spoon in the ink. You had it set on the board beside the pot, stain showing, and you left the quarrel at that size.

relations.note: she finds the spoon in her mistress's own ink-things
relations.quote: It is here. In with the ink-things.

title: Asked which caller could profit by a spoon

participation.context: Looked at the spoon on the board and left it there.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

story.body: You looked at the spoon where Alse had set it, beside the ink-pot, black to the neck.
